## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-12"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><div class="odv-at"><div class="odv-at-frame"><table class="odv-at-table"><thead><tr class="odv-at-head"><th class="chk"><span class="odv-at-box"></span></th><th class="">Record<svg class="odv-am-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m21 16-4 4-4-4"/><path d="M17 20V4"/><path d="m3 8 4-4 4 4"/><path d="M7 4v16"/></svg></th><th class="">Status</th><th class="num">Amount<svg class="odv-am-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m21 16-4 4-4-4"/><path d="M17 20V4"/><path d="m3 8 4-4 4 4"/><path d="M7 4v16"/></svg></th><th class="end"></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr class="odv-at-row"><td class="chk"><span class="odv-at-box"></span></td><td class="">REC-1042</td><td class="">Open</td><td class="num">1,240.00<i class="odv-am-n">12</i></td><td class="end"></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">12</i><b>Number cell</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you read it?">Readability</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Typography · Which text roles does it need? → Core and data</div><div class="odv-am-why">A data role keeps numbers in aligned columns.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">What is the main task? → Scan and compare</div><div class="odv-am-why">People scan rows and compare values.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For a number in a table, use type.data. Don't use type.body.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Mono digits line up in columns, so values compare at a glance.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>type.data.font-family</code><span>→</span><code>table.cell.font-family</code><span class="odv-am-val">&quot;IBM Plex Mono&quot;, ui-monospace, monospace</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> ibm-plex-mono for data text: IBM Plex Sans for every text role and IBM Plex Mono for data: exact and quiet, so the numbers stay the hero.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `data-table`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy dense-data data-table`
